chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

It is not befitting for a man to leave the perfume (on himself) on any day, so if he is unable to do so, then (on) one day and (skip) one day, so if he is unable (to do that), then (on) every Friday, and he should not leave it (completely).
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum frequency a Muslim man should use perfume according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* emphasizes the importance of personal hygiene and scent as a form of *Adab* (etiquette) and preparation for congregational prayers, reflecting the Shia emphasis on cleanliness as part of faith. The graduated approach—prioritizing daily use but allowing flexibility for alternating days or weekly Friday application—demonstrates the jurisprudential principle of *Taysir* (ease), ensuring the practice remains sustainable for the average believer. It underscores the social dimension of worship, where pleasant scent is viewed as a courtesy to others in the mosque and community.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moamar Bin Khallad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It is not befitting for the man that he should leave the perfume during each day, so if he is not able over it, so a day and a day (alternate days), so if he is not able, so during every Friday, and he should not leave it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A man must not ignore using perfumes every day, or every other day, if he cannot afford. If he cannot afford this, he must use perfume every Friday.’”
